implementation_summary: zip.ts: writeZip(entries) and sanitizeEntryName(name), built on node:zlib (deflateRawSync, crc32) with no new dependency. Names are cleaned: backslashes become /, drive letters and leading slashes are removed, '.', '..' and empty segments are dropped, and control or reserved characters become _. Entries are sorted by byte order. Each entry is deflated, or stored when deflate would not make it smaller. Timestamps are fixed, so the same input always gives the same bytes. It throws on duplicate names after cleaning, on a name with nothing usable left, and on anything that would need ZIP64. render-docx.ts: renderDocx(docs) builds one .docx by hand from the AuditDoc block model. Each document's title uses Heading1 and block heading level n uses Heading(n+1), the same mapping as render-html. Lists get one numbering instance each, so every ordered list starts at 1. Tables have a header row that repeats on each page and short rows padded. PNG/JPEG data: images are embedded with sizes read from the image header and scaled to the text width. GIF, WebP and non-data images become the imageNotIncluded label plus the alt text. Notes use a Note style. Page breaks are added for pagebreak blocks and between documents. The page is A4 with the HTML print margins. Every run carries w:lang <lang>-IN (ta-IN for Tamil, also w:bidi) and rFonts w:cs='Nirmala UI'. The font table gives 'Latha' as the fallback (w:altName). Urdu gets bidi/rtl. All text is XML-escaped, and characters XML 1.0 cannot hold are removed. render-pdf.ts: renderPdf(html, { format: 'A4', timeoutMs?, onBlockedRequest? }) starts its own Chromium through playwright. The context has JavaScript turned off, is offline and blocks service workers. context.route('**/*') aborts every request that is not data:. It then runs setContent and page.pdf({ format: 'A4', printBackground: true }). One timeout covers the browser start (Playwright's launch timeout) and a separate one covers the printing. The browser is closed in a finally block on every path. Errors are fixed plain sentences ('The document could not be printed to PDF.' or 'Printing the document to PDF took too long...'), with the original error kept only as `cause`.

risks: audit-doc-pdf.test.ts launches Chromium but is not yet listed in BROWSER_TESTS.core in vitest.workspace.ts, which this task does not own. Until G7 adds it, it runs in the 'unit' project (seen as |unit| in the run).

The Tamil PDF font test depends on the host having one of the TAMIL_FONT_STACK fonts installed. It passed on this Windows machine. A Linux CI or Cloud Run image without fonts-noto-core/fonts-taml or FreeSerif would fail it. This is a real gap in the environment, not something to relax in the test.
Heading mapping in the .docx: the document title is Heading1 and block level 1-4 is Heading2-5, matching the HTML h1/h2... mapping. This is a deliberate reading of 'Heading1..3' in the task text.
The .docx has no docProps/core.xml or settings.xml. Mammoth reads it and the parts are valid, but it has not been opened in Word.
In docx, data:image/gif and data:image/webp images are shown as the 'Image not included' label (only PNG/JPEG are embedded), while the HTML renderer embeds them.
renderPdf starts a separate Chromium for each call and does not use the shared BrowserManager. The runner should limit how many exports run at once.
handoff: Node-only modules, not exported from packages/core/src/index.ts. Import them directly: writeZip / sanitizeEntryName from packages/core/src/audit/documents/zip.ts (also usable for the export bundle; entries are { name, data: string | Uint8Array }, and it throws plain-sentence errors on duplicate names after cleaning); renderDocx(docs: AuditDoc[]): Buffer (sync, throws on an empty list) from render-docx.ts; renderPdf(renderHtml(doc), { format: 'A4', timeoutMs?, onBlockedRequest? }): Promise<Buffer> from render-pdf.ts. renderPdf error messages are fixed sentences and safe to show; do not show err.cause to users. G7 must add 'audit-doc-pdf' to BROWSER_TESTS.core in vitest.workspace.ts. Any Linux image that prints Tamil PDFs needs a Tamil font installed.
